name: Comments Anywhere for Elementor – Social Comments, Likes & More
author: Christian Wedel

sections.description:
Turn your Elementor website into a social community. Comments Anywhere for Elementor adds social-media-style comment sections, like buttons and a “my liked posts” feed as native Elementor widgets – on posts, pages, loop grids, product, course or member pages.

Visitors sign up in a popup without a page reload, comment in a mobile-friendly comment modal and like what they enjoy. More interaction, more returning visitors, more community – self-hosted on your own server.

Why Comments Anywhere?

  • Instant sign-up without page reload – AJAX login and registration modal with email verification and password reset.
  • Unlimited comment sections per page – Each widget gets its own thread, or link several widgets to one thread via a shared namespace.
  • Like button with liked-posts feed – Registered users can later see all posts they liked.
  • Built-in spam protection – Self-hosted Altcha CAPTCHA, honeypot, keyword filter and rate limiting. Akismet integration in Pro.
  • Social-media-style comment modal – Responsive popup (full screen on mobile), no scrolling back and forth.
  • Privacy-friendly – All data stays in your WordPress database. Opt-in consent snackbar and self-service account deletion.

Perfect for

  • Blogs and magazines – comments and likes under articles and in post grids
  • Membership sites – logged-in-only or private comments, personal “liked posts” area
  • Online courses – Q&A sections per lesson, several threads per page
  • WooCommerce shops – product discussions and wishlist-style favorites

Elementor widgets

  • Like Icon – like button with counter and animation; works in Loop templates.
  • Comment Icon – opens a comment modal with threaded replies and comment likes.
  • Comment Embed – always-visible inline comment section.
  • Liked Posts – posts liked by the current user, filterable by post type; Loop Grid query ID scany_liked_posts.

More features

  • Comment visibility: public, logged-in only or private
  • Edit own comments for 15 minutes, delete anytime
  • Sort by newest, oldest or most reactions
  • WordPress users are linked automatically; guest accounts with secure session cookies
  • Global design system plus per-widget style controls
  • Works with page caching (likes and comments load via REST API)
  • Integrates with the WordPress Export/Erase Personal Data tools

The plugin provides privacy building blocks but cannot make your site “GDPR-compliant” by itself. This is not legal advice; consult a legal professional.

Free vs. Pro

Free: all widgets, unlimited comment sections, likes, guest accounts with AJAX login, comment visibility, Liked Posts, Altcha CAPTCHA, consent snackbar and all design controls.

Pro: statistics, comment moderation, email notifications, custom SVG icons and Akismet integration – see commentsanywhere.com.

Documentation

  • Plugin website & Pro version
  • Documentation

Third Party Services

This plugin uses Freemius for optional usage tracking and paid-license management. Free features work when Skip is selected. Only after explicit opt-in or paid-license activation, Freemius may receive:

  • WordPress account name and email address
  • Site URL/title/language, server IP, and WordPress/PHP versions
  • Plugin/SDK versions and activation state
  • Installed plugin/theme names, versions and state if that permission is enabled
  • Paid-license status

No comments, likes, or personal visitor data are ever transmitted to Freemius. This connection is subject to the Freemius Privacy Policy and Freemius Terms of Service.

Optionally, if the site owner installs and activates the separate Akismet plugin, comment content, IP address, user agent, referrer and site URL are sent to Akismet for spam checking, subject to the Akismet Privacy Policy. This is disabled by default.

Source Code

assets/js/altcha.min.js is the minified browser build of the third-party [ALTCHA](https://altcha.org) Proof-of-Work CAPTCHA widget (MIT license), used unmodified.
  • Package: altcha v3.1.0 (npm)
  • Source: https://github.com/altcha-org/altcha/tree/7fd2468bdf60eb13670d580e80e1d70dd72909fe

  • License and build instructions: assets/js/ALTCHA-LICENSE.txt in this plugin’s own source

    assets/js/altcha-worker.js is this plugin’s own code (not third-party), a small Web Worker that runs ALTCHA’s Proof-of-Work solver off the main thread.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Elementor (the free version is enough).
  2. Install “Comments Anywhere for Elementor” via Plugins → Add New (or upload it to /wp-content/plugins/soulsites-comments-anywhere/) and activate it.
  3. Drag the Like Icon, Comment Icon, Comment Embed or Liked Posts widget onto any Elementor page.
  4. Adjust options under Soulsites Comments Anywhere → Settings.

See the documentation for details.
sections.faq:
How do I add comments to an Elementor page?

Drag the Comment Icon (popup) or Comment Embed (inline section) widget onto the page. No shortcodes or theme changes needed.

Can I add multiple comment sections on one page?

Yes. Use different namespaces for independent threads, or the same namespace to show one thread in several places.

Do visitors need to reload the page to register?

No. Registration, login and password reset run in an AJAX popup.

Can users see the posts they liked?

Yes, via the Liked Posts widget or an Elementor Pro Loop Grid with the query ID scany_liked_posts.

Do I need Elementor Pro?

No. Elementor Pro is only needed for the Loop Grid integration.

Is it GDPR friendly?

It is self-hosted, shows an opt-in consent snackbar, deletes unused anonymous identifiers after 1 year, lets users delete their account and integrates with WordPress privacy tools. Compliance also depends on your own configuration and privacy policy.

How does spam protection work?

Free includes a self-hosted Altcha CAPTCHA, honeypot, keyword filter and rate limiting. Pro adds Akismet (requires the Akismet plugin).

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. Personal like status and comments load client-side, so page caches never store them.

Is all data deleted on uninstall?

Yes. All plugin tables, options, transients and cron events are removed.
